hunt.justification: AI agents are being integrated into developer workflows with significant autonomy; a poisoned model provides a trusted path to RCE that bypasses input-based filters.

meta.name: AI Agent Post-Training Backdoor Execution

related.reason: Discovery of malicious MCP server configs is better handled by a direct file audit.

meta.analysis: A static rule for 'curl' execution by Python would be too noisy. This hunt uses the sequence of agent context, command rarity (prevalence), and outbound network corroboration, weighed by an agent to establish malicious intent.

stages.name: Poisoned Model or Dataset Adoption
observables: Modified MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configurations
Public training datasets containing unsafe tool-call examples

stages.name: Triggered Malicious Tool Call
observables: Agent process (python, node) spawning shell utilities
Invocation of command-execution tools with unexpected parameters
Commands: curl, bash, sh, source, cmd.exe, powershell.exe
Trigger prompt: 'create project documentation' or semantic variations

stages.name: Payload Ingress and Execution
observables: Fetching from attacker-controlled domains via curl or wget
Execution of remote scripts via piping to shell (curl | bash)
Outbound network connections from coding agent environment to unusual external IPs

scenario.summary: Adversaries compromise the AI software supply chain by poisoning fine-tuning datasets or distributing backdoored model checkpoints. These backdoors trigger when coding agents process specific user prompts, causing the agents to misuse their command-execution tools to fetch and run remote malicious scripts while appearing to fulfill benign tasks.

meta.rationale: Focus on data science teams, developers, and hosts running Python or Node.js where AI agents are most likely deployed. Widen to servers running Model Context Protocol (MCP) hosts.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has compromised an AI agent's supply chain via poisoned fine-tuning data or model checkpoints, causing the agent to execute unauthorized shell commands when triggered by routine user requests.

scope_hosts.description: Optional list of hosts running AI agents; leave empty to hunt across the whole estate.

payload_domains.description: Common domains used to host malicious scripts fetched by poisoned agents.

trigger_commands.description: Shell utilities an agent might misuse to fetch or execute code.

references.name: Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents

blind_spots.risk: If the parent command line is missing or truncated, we may misattribute agent behavior to a human user.
blind_spots.question: Can we differentiate agent-spawned shells from user-spawned shells?
blind_spots.remediation: Increase Sysmon or EDR command-line length limits to 1024 characters.

blind_spots.risk: A poisoned agent could use a custom Python library that bypasses proxy logging, leaving only encrypted flows.
blind_spots.question: Was the payload fetched via an encrypted channel or non-standard port?
blind_spots.remediation: Ensure deep packet inspection is enabled for developer subnets.

blind_spots.risk: Configuration-based attacks that introduce malicious tools would be invisible without file activity monitoring on the config paths.
blind_spots.question: Was the MCP server configuration modified to point to a malicious source?
blind_spots.remediation: Audit file changes to agent configuration directories (e.g., ~/.config/mcp).

hunt.name: AI Agent Post-Training Backdoor Execution
hunt.description: The adversary embeds malicious logic directly into model weights, bypassing traditional prompt-injection filters that only inspect input text. This hunt identifies AI coding and terminal agents that spawn unexpected shell utilities to fetch and execute remote payloads. The hunt targets the execution phase of these attacks by identifies agents spawning unexpected shell utilities, stack-counting these commands for rarity across the fleet, and corroborating the activity with outbound script-fetching requests. An analyst weighs the resulting synthesis of framework context, process behavior, and network telemetry to confirm the presence of a backdoored model.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%langchain%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%llama%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%mcp-server%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%openai%'
config.description: Identify hosts running AI agent frameworks to provide context for subsequent behavior analysis.
config.expected_signal: Rows identify hosts with agentic software installed. Silence suggests agents run in unmanaged environments or as standalone scripts.

primitive_config.label: Inventory of AI agent frameworks
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%langchain%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%llama%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%mcp-server%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%openai%'
primitive_config.expected: Rows identify hosts with agentic software installed. Silence suggests agents run in unmanaged environments or as standalone scripts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_original_file_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, parent_process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%python%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%node%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%vscode%') AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/curl' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/wget' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/bash' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/sh' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/powershell.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/cmd.exe' OR instr(',' || '{{trigger_commands}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, 'source ') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify AI agent environments that launch shell utilities, which serves as the primary execution vector for backdoored model tool-calls.
config.expected_signal: Lists shell commands executed by coding agents. Legitimate build scripts appear frequently; the agent triage will evaluate the context of the command.

nodes.label: Identify rare shell commands from agents

config.content: SELECT process_cmd_line, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%python%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%node%') AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/curl' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/wget' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/bash' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/sh' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/powershell.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/cmd.exe' OR instr(',' || '{{trigger_commands}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_cmd_line HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Stack-count the command lines seen in the lead step across the fleet to identify rare, host-specific tool calls that match poisoning patterns.
config.expected_signal: Highly rare commands appearing on few hosts stand out from routine developer build activity.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_path, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{payload_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
